metadata.title: MAGNUS magnetized neutron-star atmosphere tables: specific intensity on grids of field strength, temperature, gravity and field inclination

creators.name: de Lima, Rafael C. R.
creators.affiliation: Universidade do Estado de Santa Catarina (UDESC); ICRANet, Universita degli Studi di Ferrara

metadata.description:
Tables of emergent specific intensity from magnetized, fully ionized hydrogen neutron-star atmospheres, computed with MAGNUS. They are the atmosphere input for spectral and pulse-profile fitting of thermally emitting isolated neutron stars.

Each table is a binary file in the MAGNUSI2 format: an 8-byte magic string, then six axes written as a 32-bit count followed by that many 32-bit floats (lg B, lg T, lg g, theta_B, mu, lg E), then the intensity block. Units are log10(B/G), log10(T_eff/K), log10(g/cm s^-2), degrees, cosine of the emission angle, and log10(E/keV). The accompanying MANIFEST.json carries the exact axes, sizes and SHA-256 of every file; README.md carries the physics and the provenance of each grid.

Contents

FileGrid (lg B x lg T x lg g x theta_B)ModelsVacuum polarization
magnus_campoBg_denso_v2.magnus15 x 7 x 3 x 3945no
magnus_campoBg_denso_v2_atom.magnus15 x 7 x 3 x 3945no, partial ionization
magnus_campoBg_denso_v3.magnus17 x 9 x 5 x 32295no
magnus_campoBg_vacuo_v4.magnus17 x 9 x 9 x 34131yes

All share 8 emission angles and 160 energies spanning 0.03-20 keV.

Physics

The v2 tables introduced the quantizing Coulomb logarithm in the cyclic components of free-free absorption (Eq. 44 of Potekhin & Chabrier 2003). Validation against the Rosseland means of that work and the monochromatic opacities of Suleimanov, Potekhin & Werner (2009) had shown the X mode to be 3-6 times too transparent at lg B >= 13 without it.

The v3 table extends the v2 axes without changing the physics: cells shared with v2 are byte-for-byte identical. The axes were extended because fits were running into the v2 boundaries in field, gravity and temperature.

The v4 table is the first with vacuum polarization, mode labelling by ellipticity and a direct integrator, and it doubles the gravity resolution to 0.1 dex. Measured against v3 at lg g 14.4, lg T 5.9-6.1, over 0.15-1.0 keV, the median intensity change is 0.2 % at lg B 13.30, 0.5 % at 13.55, 5.0 % at 13.85 and 7.3 % at 14.00, with p90 reaching 70 % and 126 % at the two highest fields. Vacuum polarization is therefore not negligible for sources with lg B around 13.85, and the small-effect estimate from Eq. 5 of van Adelsberg & Lai (2006) underestimates it.

Quality

Flux-conservation error per model in v4: median 1.0 %, p90 3.1 %, with 1.7 % of models above 10 % and 5 above 30 %. The poor tail sits entirely in the hot, high-field corner (lg B >= 13.9 with lg T >= 6.20). Clamping at |lg w| = 30 affects 15.8 % of cells, all above 3 keV where the ratio to the Planck function overflows in the Wien tail; within 0.15-1.0 keV it is 0.03 %.

How to cite

Please cite this dataset and the MAGNUS code (concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22760147) separately, and name the table by file and SHA-256 as recorded in MANIFEST.json.
metadata.notes: Generated by scripts/tabela_campo_g_denso.py and merged with scripts/mesclar_tabelas.py. Regeneration cost: about 5.3 h per model on one core of the AMD EPYC nodes of the sci-com cluster (UFES), 1.6 h on the development desktop, with a 0.43 GB memory peak per model for the vacuum branch.
